method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of the total-versus-partial diagonal argument and exercise, with exact formula, macro and reference parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Impossibility of a total universal computable function, diagonal proof, partial-universal contrast and the self-application exercise.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A partial computable evaluator can be universal for partial computable functions, but no total computable evaluator is universal for all total computable functions. If Un' were total and computable, d(x)=Un'(x,x)+1 would be total computable and would disagree with its kth row at x=k for every k.
